title: Someone at home is becoming dangerous
lede: The pattern is now familiar. The mood turns, the accusations start, the doors get blocked, objects get thrown or broken. You have started managing your own behaviour continuously to prevent the next episode.

blocks.text: The pattern is now familiar. The mood turns, the accusations start, the doors get blocked, objects get thrown or broken. You have started managing your own behaviour continuously to prevent the next episode.

items: Escalation over time is the single most reliable predictor in this situation. The incidents do not usually plateau on their own, and the apology phase is part of the cycle rather than a break from it.
The behaviour is not caused by what you did or failed to do. The rules change precisely so that they cannot be satisfied — that is the mechanism of control, not a failure of your compliance.
The period around leaving is statistically the most dangerous. This is not an argument for staying; it is an argument for leaving with a plan rather than in the middle of an incident.

Certain markers correlate strongly with serious harm: strangulation at any point, threats to kill, weapons in the house, stalking, jealousy-driven monitoring, threats about children or pets, and escalation during pregnancy or after separation. If any are present, treat this as urgent rather than ongoing.

items.move: During an incident, do not argue the facts
items.detail: Reduce stimulus. Agree with whatever is cheap. Your objective inside the episode is only to get through it without injury.

items.move: Keep yourself out of enclosed rooms
items.detail: Stay near an exit. Avoid kitchens and bathrooms — hard surfaces, hard objects, no way past. Do not let yourself be positioned away from the door.

items.move: Have a go-bag somewhere outside the house
items.detail: At a friend's, at work, in a locker. Documents, medication, spare keys, cash, chargers, copies of children's papers. Inside the house it can be found and used as leverage.

items.move: Set up a code word with two people
items.detail: One text or one word that means call for help now and do not reply with questions.

items.move: Document quietly and store it externally
items.detail: Dates, photographs of injuries, screenshots of messages, medical visits. In a cloud account they do not know exists, or with someone you trust. Never on the shared device.

items.move: Call a domestic abuse service before you need to leave
items.detail: They do safety planning for exactly this, confidentially, and they know what the local protections actually are. This is planning, not commitment.

items.say: Whatever ends it. "Okay." "You're right." "I'm sorry." These are tools, not concessions, and using them is not weakness.
Agreed in advance, e.g. "Did you find my blue jacket?" — meaning: call the police to my address now.

items.when: To emergency services when you cannot speak freely
items.say: Many services support a silent call procedure. Learn your local one now. Otherwise: state the address first and leave the line open.
"I am not safe at home." That sentence opens a support pathway everywhere in healthcare.

items: Announcing that you are leaving, mid-incident. That is the highest-risk moment to disclose a plan.
Keeping the evidence on a device they can access, or in a shared account.
Accepting that the calm, remorseful phase proves it has ended. Measure the pattern over months, not the current mood.
Handling it entirely alone to protect their reputation or the family's image. Isolation is the condition this behaviour needs to continue.
Waiting for physical injury to count it as real. Control, threats, financial restriction and monitoring are the same phenomenon.
Get legal information about occupation and protective orders, and about children, from someone specialist. General advice from friends is often wrong in ways that cost you.
Change passwords, check devices and cars for tracking, and turn off location sharing you forgot existed — including on shared accounts and family plans.
Assume the story told about you afterwards will be unflattering. Your documentation matters more than your explanations.
Get support for yourself specifically. The recalibration of what is normal takes real time and is much harder alone.

limit: If you are in immediate danger, call emergency services now. If strangulation has ever happened, if there are weapons in the house, or if there have been threats to kill, treat this as an emergency and contact a domestic abuse service or the police today — not when it next happens. These markers are associated with the most serious outcomes.
